title: AI crawler rules are explicit
question: Does robots.txt state a decision for each major AI training crawler?
method: For GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot, CCBot, Bytespider and Applebot-Extended, record whether robots.txt names the agent. Pass when all are named (allowed or disallowed); warn when some are; fail when none are. The verdict is per bot in the evidence.

title: Shopping agents are not blocked
question: May user-triggered shopping agents fetch product pages?
method: Evaluate robots.txt for ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, OAI-SearchBot, Google-Agent and Perplexity-User against a sampled product path. Fail when any is disallowed; pass otherwise.

title: Content Signals declared
question: Does the site state how its content may be used by AI systems?
method: Look for Content-Signal: lines in robots.txt or a Content-Signal response header with ai-train, search or ai-input values. Pass when present and parseable.

title: No WAF challenge for agent profiles
question: Do agent user agents get the same product page a browser gets?
method: Fetch one product page with a browser baseline and up to six agent user-agent strings. Compare status code and extracted main text. Fail on a challenge page, 403 or cloaked content for any agent profile; warn on minor differences.

title: Web Bot Auth key directory
question: Does the site publish a key directory so signed agent requests can be verified?
method: GET /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory. Informational: pass when a JWKS-shaped document is served, otherwise warn without penalty beyond weight 1.

title: No noindex or nosnippet on product pages
question: Do product pages allow indexing and snippets?
method: Read X-Robots-Tag headers and meta robots tags on sampled product pages. Fail on noindex; warn on nosnippet, noai or max-snippet:0.
